findings.text: Provides a global query that reports whether a stable node can accept further sharing for a given additional offset, requiring at least one existing mapping and a total below the configured maximum.
Provides a global query that reports whether a stable node can accept further sharing with no additional offset, delegating to the offset aware variant.

Detachment of a stable flagged reverse mapping entry removes its hash list linkage while holding the backing folio locked, then releases lock and reference, decrements either the sharing or shared global counter depending on whether siblings remain, decrements the owning address space merging count and the node mapping length, releases the anon vma reference, clears the linear index and head linkage, and normalizes the address to a page boundary.

Detachment of an unstable flagged entry derives an age from the difference between the global scan sequence and the stored address, requires that age to be zero or one, erases the red black node from the per node unstable root only when age is zero, decrements the unshared global counter, and normalizes the address to a page boundary.
Trailing cleanup walks the singly linked list of reverse mapping entries, detaching each entry from its tree before freeing its container, until the list head becomes empty.

Stable node removal treats a missing or already detached backing folio as success, otherwise fails with busy status when the folio remains mapped, and on an unmapped folio clears the folio back pointer and removes the node from the stable tree before unlocking and dropping the reference.

Chain aware removal handles a single node by delegating to single removal and converting the error status to a boolean, while a chain container iterates safely over duplicate members and aborts on the first busy member, asserting emptiness before freeing the container.

Full teardown iterates over each node identifier root, repeatedly removing the current first tree entry and advancing to the next identifier on busy status, then processes the migration list similarly, yielding the processor during long loops and returning busy if any member remained.

Mass unmerge visits address space slots in list order, breaks sharing only inside mergeable areas that have an anon vma, removes trailing reverse mapping entries, retires slots whose address space is exiting by unlinking and freeing the slot plus clearing mergeable flags and dropping a reference, cleans stable nodes on a best effort basis, and resets the global scan sequence.
Slot lookup derives the enclosing KSM slot structure address from the address of its embedded generic member using container address arithmetic.
Checksum computation temporarily maps a page into local address space, hashes the full page content with a fixed zero seed, unmaps, and returns the resulting word.

Write protection rejects compound folios, resolves the virtual address inside the given area, brackets the reverse mapping walk with a notifier clear range, requires a present leaf entry, and when the entry is writable or dirty or exclusive or a flush is pending it flushes the cache, clears and flushes the entry before validating references, shares exclusive anonymous state, propagates dirtiness to the folio, then installs a clean non writable entry and reports the final entry to the caller.

Replacement resolves the virtual address, requires a present non huge middle directory entry observed without locking, brackets the update with a notifier clear range, requires the current leaf entry to match the previously captured entry while holding the table lock, then either establishes a referenced anonymous mapping for a normal shared page or installs a special dirty marker for the zero page with adjustment of zero mapping and anonymous accounting, flushes cache, clears and flushes the old entry, installs the new entry, removes the old reverse mapping, frees swap when unmapped, and drops a reference.

Single page merge is a no operation when source and target are identical, requires an anonymous folio, proceeds only when a non blocking folio lock succeeds, splits compound folios before continuing, write protects the folio, then either promotes the folio to a KSM owned state with accessed and dirty marking when no target exists or replaces the mapping only after verifying identical content.

Zero page merge proceeds only when the global zero page mode is enabled and the stored old checksum equals the empty page checksum, looks up a mergeable area at the stored address under read lock, attempts a merge with the architecture zero page for that address, treats a missing area as success, and emits a trace record.

Merge with a KSM page looks up a mergeable area under read lock, attempts a single page merge, and on success first detaches the reverse mapping entry from the unstable tree then captures the anon vma with an added reference plus the linear page index while still holding the lock, before the entry can join the stable tree, and emits a trace record.

Two page merge first creates a new KSM page from the first entry with no target, then merges the second entry onto the first, breaking copy on write of the first when the second merge fails, and returns the first folio on full success or null on failure.
Sharing candidacy asserts a non negative mapping length and holds exactly when the length is positive and the sum of length plus the supplied offset remains below the global maximum sharing limit.

Duplicate selection optionally gates stale pruning by elapsed time since the last prune against a configured millisecond interval, safely walks duplicate members skipping stale entries whose folio disappeared, retains the best candidate preferring sharing capable entries with larger mapping counts, collapses the chain into a single node when only one member remains with adjustment of chain and duplicate counters, moves a reusable non head member to the head when it can accept two further merges, and frees the whole chain when no candidate remains.
Chain access returns the backing folio directly for a non chain node, otherwise delegates to duplicate selection with stale pruning enabled for the pruning variant and disabled for the plain variant.

Stable search short circuits with an added folio reference when the folio already owns a non migration stable node, otherwise selects the stable root for the folio NUMA node, walks the tree comparing full page content to descend left or right, prunes each visited chain, restarts from the root when a stale node may have rebalanced the tree, and on content equality diverts migrated folios with multiple mappings toward chain append while rejecting matches whose duplicate cannot accept sharing.
Stable flagged detachment holds the backing folio lock across hash list removal and keeps the lock until after list mutation, then unlocks and drops the folio reference.
Single stable node removal holds the backing folio lock across the mapped check and the back pointer clear plus tree removal, then unlocks and drops the reference on all paths that acquired a folio.

Mass unmerge holds the global mmlist spinlock only while advancing the scan cursor between slots, holds the address space read lock across area iteration and sharing break plus trailing cleanup, and checks the exiting flag under read lock to avoid unsafe maple tree interaction.

Write protection surrounds the reverse mapping walk with notifier range start and end for a clear operation over one page, completes the walk before ending the notifier, and performs table clear plus TLB flush before validating reference counts so that direct I/O cannot interleave after the check.

Replacement surrounds the leaf update with notifier range start and end for a clear operation over one page, acquires the page table lock for leaf mapping, validates entry sameness while locked, and releases via table unmap unlock on all locked paths.
Single page merge uses a non blocking folio lock attempt and abandons the page when the lock is busy, holding the lock across write protection and promotion or replacement when acquired.

Zero page and KSM page merges acquire the address space read lock before area lookup and hold it across the merge attempt and, for the KSM variant, across unstable detachment plus anon vma capture, releasing before tracing.
Replacement observes the middle directory entry with a lockless read and validates presence plus non huge status before acquiring the leaf table lock.

Reverse mapping entry as observed carries a flagged address combining page address with stable and unstable indicators, a head pointer to a stable node, hash list and tree node linkages, a NUMA identifier, an anon vma pointer sharing storage with unstable state, a linear page index, a singly linked list pointer, an owning address space pointer, and a stored old checksum.

Stable node as observed carries a tree node linkage, a hash list of mappings or duplicates with a duplicate linkage variant, a signed mapping length count, a list linkage for migration handling, a head indicator distinguishing migration membership, and a timestamp for chain prune gating.

Address space slot tracking as observed embeds a generic slot holding an address space pointer and a list node inside a KSM slot that also holds a trailing reverse mapping list, with a global list head and a scan cursor advanced under lock.

Reverse mapping entry lifecycle has a stable attached state flagged stable and linked into a stable hash list, an unstable attached state flagged unstable and linked into a per node tree with scan age zero or one, and a detached state with normalized page address plus cleared head and index. Removal transitions either attached state to detached.

Stable node organization has single, chain container, and duplicate member forms. A singular chain collapses to single, a reusable duplicate can move to chain head, and an empty or fully stale chain is freed, while removal of a chain requires successful removal of every duplicate.

Merge lifecycle proceeds from address lookup to write protection, then either to promotion of an anonymous folio into a new stable entry or to content comparison followed by replacement with an existing shared page. The two page variant sequences promotion of the first entry before sharing of the second, with rollback via copy on write break on partial failure.

Stable lookup traversal starts with a fork shortcut, then per node root selection, then a loop of prune plus content compare with left or right descent, restart on stale rebalance, and terminal handling of content equality via chain append diversion, sharing rejection, or locked folio return.

Mass unmerge lifecycle iterates slots in order through lock acquisition, exiting check, per area sharing break, trailing cleanup and unlock, then slot retirement for exiting spaces, finishing with best effort stable cleanup and scan sequence reset, with an early error path that releases locks and resets the scan cursor to the head.
Sharing candidacy queries serve as externally callable predicates for merge admission, one accepting an offset for future merge accounting and one checking current state with zero offset.
Stable tree search serves as the scanner lookup entry that maps a candidate page to a shareable stable folio or null when no reusable match exists in the observed prefix.
Two page merge and single page with target variants serve as scanner facing merge drivers that coordinate area lookup, protection, replacement, and stable linkage.

Address space exit can race mass teardown and stable removal. The code refuses configuration changing removal when a folio remains mapped and checks the exiting flag under read lock before walking areas.

Direct I/O without locks can raise folio references concurrently with write protection. Clearing and flushing the table entry before comparing reference count against mapping count plus swap cache presence closes the window, restoring the old entry on mismatch.

Compound and huge mappings require special handling. Write protection fails on large folios, single merge splits huge pages first, and replacement aborts when the middle directory entry is missing or huge or not present.

Stale stable entries can be freed and rebalance the tree during lookup. Search restarts from the root after encountering a vanished chain member, and duplicate walks use safe iteration that tolerates concurrent freeing.
Long scans and teardowns can monopolize the processor. Detachment, full stable teardown, duplicate selection, and tree search yield at regular points.

Exclusive anonymous state affects sharing safety. Write protection attempts to share exclusive state before proceeding and restores the old entry on failure, while replacement asserts absence of exclusivity on both source and shared anonymous folios.
Page table entries can change between capture and replacement. The code rechecks leaf sameness under lock and aborts on mismatch, on non present entries, or on unexpected middle directory mappings.
